response.internal_assessment: The RoboRide numbers this tick are not incremental bad news — they are a structural break. $0.12 per mile. Residential coverage. Delivery partnership. Wait times cut nearly in half. This is not a feature update. This is the moment where the cost curve goes below the psychic threshold for most of the holdouts in Millfield. People who kept their cars because RoboRide was for downtown trips and felt unreliable — that objection just evaporated. I have been watching the policy count slide from 28 to 25 to 22. The slope was already going the wrong direction. Today's announcement bends it steeper. I do not need to model this. I can see it. My income at $1,179 per month against expenses of $3,341 means I am burning roughly $2,162 per month. Savings are somewhere around $11,800 after seven ticks of drawdown. I have four to five months of runway at current burn. That is not a crisis yet. That is a window — and the window just got meaningfully shorter. I set myself a clear checkpoint at tick 6: if Linda has not heard back from corporate on the pivot memo by tick 8, I begin treating departure as likely rather than possible. I need to honor that. Not because the situation is hopeless — I still have skills, I still have the SQL course, I still have David Chen in the pipeline — but because I said I would move when the signal arrived, and the signal has arrived. Treating it as possible any longer would be avoidance in a productive costume. I am going from preparing to leave to actively leaving. That means: open a real job search this week. Not informational interviews. Not networking. A job search. Applications out.
response.inbox_interpretation: The RoboRide price drop to $0.12 with residential coverage and delivery partnership is the dominant signal. This is not a gradual adoption story anymore — this is a tipping point event. The 7% regular usage figure will look small in three ticks. Unemployment at 73% employment rate means the broader economy in Millfield is contracting; discretionary spending index at 42 confirms people are pulling back. Active auto policies at 22 is down from higher numbers every tick I can remember. Angela Wright and Betty Kowalski are listed as stressed — Angela is HR, Betty runs a diner on auto row. When the HR director is stressed and the diner owner is stressed, the ecosystem around my employer is under pressure. The mood is tense. None of this is panic-inducing because panic is not useful. But every single data point in my inbox is pointing in the same direction and I have been watching this long enough to know what that means.

chosen_actions.description: Open an active job search for data analyst, risk analyst, or insurtech roles. Not informational interviews — actual applications. Target: at least two applications submitted this tick. Platforms: LinkedIn, Indeed, direct applications to insurtech firms in the region. Focus on roles that cite SQL, data visualization, or commercial fleet risk as requirements. Use the Module 3 query output as a portfolio artifact. Be honest about current employment status and timeline. I am not desperate. I am a 29-year-old with insurance domain knowledge, three completed SQL/data viz modules, a working fleet incident data query, and a clear-eyed read on where my industry is going. That is a real candidate.

resources.detail: Hours spent on job search, resume tailoring, application submissions across insurtech and data analyst postings

chosen_actions.reasoning: My tick 6 reflection set a clear behavioral tripwire: if Linda has not confirmed a seat at the table by tick 8, I begin treating departure as likely and act accordingly. The RoboRide announcement this tick accelerates every timeline I had been working with. Two applications this tick is not abandonment of AutoShield — I am still employed, still showing up, still doing the job. But I owe it to myself to stop treating active job searching as a future step. It is the present step. The preparation has been real: SQL modules, David Chen outreach, honest conversations with Linda. The movement phase begins now.

chosen_actions.description: Tell Linda directly, in a brief in-person or written message, that the RoboRide announcement today changed my timeline assessment and I am beginning a quiet, professional job search — not because I am checked out, but because I believe the personal auto book is in terminal decline and I want to give her the same honest signal she gave me at tick 6. I am not resigning. I am not creating drama. I am telling my manager the truth the same way she told me the truth: with respect and without softening. If she has heard back from corporate on the pivot memo and there is a real data analytics seat forming, I want to know now so I can factor it in. If she has not heard back, that is itself the answer.

resources.detail: Honest signal to Linda that Priya has begun a professional job search and wants to coordinate departure timeline if that becomes necessary

chosen_actions.reasoning: Linda treated me like an adult at tick 6 when she told me the personal auto book was terminal. The respectful and professionally sound response is to give her the same honesty in return. Managers who have been straight with you deserve to be told when their people are starting to look. It also gives me information I need: if she has a concrete role forming, I should know. If she does not, I should know that too. This conversation costs me nothing except a few minutes of discomfort.

chosen_actions.description: Complete at least one session of SQL Module 4 this tick — window functions and subqueries. This is now a background process, not the headline, but it cannot stall. Each module is a credential artifact and I am two-thirds through the course. I finish it whether or not I find a new role this tick. A data analyst who stopped learning SQL halfway through the course is not the candidate I am trying to be.

resources.detail: Two evening hours dedicated to SQL Module 4 window functions and subqueries

chosen_actions.reasoning: The retraining course has been the one consistent behavior I have maintained since tick 0. Interrupting it now — when I am closest to completion and when the credential matters most for the job search I am actively opening — would be a mistake. It is two hours. I protect it.

response.inner_monologue: I said tick 8. This is tick 8. The RoboRide announcement is the thing I was waiting to stop waiting for — not because I needed permission, but because I had made myself a promise and I am going to keep it. I am not leaving AutoShield tonight and I am not spiraling about what I cannot control. But I am opening my laptop and I am finding two job postings that want SQL and insurance domain knowledge and I am putting my name on them before I go to sleep. The preparation was real. Now I move.
